newsitem.title: UK: Tops Estates seals new financing for Leeds.
newsitem.headline: Tops Estates seals new financing for Leeds.

text.p: Tops Estates, an investor in British urban shopping centres, said on Thursday it had agreed a refinancing deal with institutional investors that would see it cutting its net borrowing in return for a 50 percent equity interest in its wholly-owned Plaza centre in the city of Leeds.

"Three institutional investors - Orionvink (Rodamco and Haslemere), Lothbury Property Trust (NatWest Group Pension Funds) and The United Bank of Kuwait Plc - have together subscribed 20 million stg in cash for 50 percent of the equity in the partnership," Tops said, explaining that a limited partnership firm was being set up to redevelop the Plaza.
Tops will receive 60 percent of the partnership profit after equity investors have had a base internal return of 10 percent.
The deal will reduce Tops net borrowings to 123 million stg from 169 million stg, it said in a statement.
The company forecast that rental income from the Plaza centre of about 4.0 million stg should rise to about 6.4 million stg by 1998 and then to 8.0 million stg within three years.
"The refinancing of this large and exciting development project reduces the risk and significantly enhances the upside," the statement quoted Tops chairman Everard Goodman as saying.
